comparison.objective: Candidate commissions and locks a robot-axis shock absorber through iterative impact testing; pr-1096 uncaps an IV bag, inserts and locks a giving-set spike, and primes a drip chamber.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed hex-key engagement, captive-set-screw loosening/relocking, fine collar rotation, counterholding, and response-guided adjustment. pr-1096 requires bimanual bag stabilization, cap pulling, aligned spike insertion, and chamber squeezing.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires a physically retained setting and two safe dynamic stops within published energy, velocity, and 12 mm stroke constraints, with no hard-stop strike, overload, excessive rebound, or drift. pr-1096 requires the spike fully locked, the chamber one-third to two-thirds full, the bag retained, release, and arm retreat. Its spec supplies insertion, fill, clearance, and timing thresholds; it does not test damper tuning or stopping behavior.
comparison.reason: The shared bimanual stabilization and tool/part alignment are generic primitives. The tested abilities and outcomes differ materially: iterative mechanical damping adjustment and retention under impacts versus irreversible medical-port insertion and simulated priming.
